title: Battle of Hattin
summary: On 4 July 1187 Saladin's army destroyed the Latin army of Guy of Lusignan, King of Jerusalem, at the Horns of Hattin near Lake Tiberias. Mounted archers wore the Franks down with thirst and harassment; the True Cross was captured and captured Templars and Hospitallers were reportedly executed. Saladin went on to take Acre and, on 2 October 1187 by one account, Jerusalem, which prompted the Third Crusade.

uncertainty.note: EBSCO gives 4 July 1187; World History Encyclopedia gives 3-4 July 1187.

as_recorded.value: On 3 July 1187 CE Saladin attacked the moving Frankish army; on the morning of 4 July the Franks tried to push on

where.modern_name: Horns of Hattin, near Tiberias, Israel
where.historical_name: Horns of Hattin (Hattin, Galilee), Kingdom of Jerusalem

importance.justification: The crusader field army was destroyed and most of the Latin kingdom, including Jerusalem, was lost within months.

audience_note: Mentions the execution of prisoners after the battle.

related.because: The Latin defeat left the kingdom undefended and Saladin took Jerusalem in autumn 1187.
